I\nitself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /proje

cts/{projectId}/eval-suites`
lists its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key

## Errors
\
nErrors always use the canonical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is huma

n-readable and may change;
`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZ
ED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth gran
t; distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on
this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine; see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |
\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allowed to do this, or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam pres
ented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | M
alformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn
't in a state that accepts this write, such as a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currentl
y be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `
RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests; see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to th
e target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |\n| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500

| Something failed on our side |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unl

ess the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on

a protected
call. The API never starts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `to
ols/call`: the API answers\n `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_40
1`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carryi
ng `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unc
hanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (`source:\n \"tool_result_meta\"`). A field the server already set under that name

is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different
key will not help. Com
plete the OAuth flow for that server yourself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n

[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests
per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.\nExceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in\nsecond

s):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED"

ff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the preview.

Other `429`s, the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described wi
th the\nendpoints below, carry `Retry-After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a
hint that is usually there\nrather than a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour backoff, so **never*

* block waiting for a header that may not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented (request and response schemas

, examples,
and an interactive playground) under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog**: discover the IDs everything else t

akes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |
| `GET /organizations` | The organiza
tions the caller belongs to, where `organizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n
| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The pro
ject's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first
: captures of its tools and server info, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers
/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in
`droppedFields` were too large to store, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisi
ons/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and serv
er info changes with both values. A field listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that side, so a c
hange to it is unknown |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |\n| `G
ET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELET
E /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}` | Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `P
OST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/servers` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacement; omitted servers are
detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GE
T /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions (`?projectId=&status=&limit=&before=`) |\n\n**Project environments**: the named execution bundle
s (one host, optionally a\nstandalone server group) that eval suites and goals run against. Reads need\nproject membership. Archiv
ing needs project admin and is revisioned: pass the\n`revision` you last read back as `expectedRevision`, and a stale value return

s
`CONFLICT` (409).

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?
includeArchived=true` to include archived ones) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environme
nt |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` | Preview the host config and closed server set this envi
ronment resolves to right now |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it. The environment
is kept, and its name is freed for a new one |\n\n**Server diagnostics & primitives** (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/

...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot |
\n| `POST .../doctor` | Full health workflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oauth` | Does this
server require an OAuth grant? |\n| `POST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; return
s the MCP `CallToolResult` plus additive `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challeng
es](#sign-in-challenges)) |\n| `POST .../prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render a prompt; retur
ns the MCP `GetPromptResult` verbatim |\n| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |\n| `POST .../resources/read` | Rea
d one resource by URI |\n| `POST .../export` | One JSON snapshot of tools, resources, and prompts |\n| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DEL
ETE .../accounts[/{account}]` | The server's accounts. See [Server accounts](#server-accounts) |\n| `POST .../oauth/import-tokens`
| **Deprecated.** Uploads to your default account; use `PUT .../accounts/{account}`. See [The deprecated import route](#the-depre

cated-import-route) |

**Eval runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-
suites` | Author-only: create a suite + its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it
